generic.title: Unauthorized value or right transfer
generic.invariant: Only an authorized lifecycle transition may move protocol value or rights.
generic.case_prompt: Identify the exact authorization decision, the state it trusts, and every path that can shape that state.
generic.attacker_goal: Cause value or rights to move without satisfying the intended authorization conditions.

generic.title: Economic accounting diverges from reality
generic.invariant: All representations of the same economic fact remain synchronized.
generic.case_prompt: Name coupled variables, live balances, caches, checkpoints, and later consumers.
generic.attacker_goal: Create a favorable divergence that a later operation treats as authoritative.

generic.title: Lifecycle or privilege bypass
generic.invariant: State transitions occur only in the allowed order and under the required role.
generic.case_prompt: Map alternate entrypoints, cancellation, partial completion, failure, and replay paths.
generic.attacker_goal: Reach a privileged or terminal state without completing its prerequisites.

generic.title: Permanent or economically meaningful denial of service
generic.invariant: Permissionless actions cannot permanently block required protocol exits or settlement.
generic.case_prompt: Identify the blocked operation, who can trigger the block, cost, duration, and recovery authority.
generic.attacker_goal: Prevent exits, settlement, liquidation, or accounting progress at acceptable cost.

vault.title: Share dilution or exchange-rate manipulation
vault.invariant: Share issuance and redemption preserve proportional ownership of economically owned assets.
vault.case_prompt: Locate totalAssets/totalSupply authorities, donation paths, virtual offsets, rounding direction, and stale balance sources.
vault.attacker_goal: Acquire excess shares or redeem more assets by manipulating the conversion decision.

vault.title: Withdrawal shortfall or selective loss socialization
vault.invariant: A valid redemption receives its fair claim without shifting losses to other holders.
vault.case_prompt: Trace request, queue, settlement, liquidity sourcing, loss recognition, and partial fulfillment.
vault.attacker_goal: Exit before losses are recognized or force remaining holders to absorb the shortfall.

vault.title: Capture of yield earned before entry
vault.invariant: New shares cannot claim yield economically earned before their capital entered.
vault.case_prompt: Map checkpoints, delayed rate updates, dormant accrual, fee realization, and deposit timing.
vault.attacker_goal: Enter immediately before a delayed accrual/checkpoint and capture historical yield.

vault.title: Loss, debt, or fee accounting desynchronization
vault.invariant: Assets, liabilities, realized losses, debt, and fees describe the same economic state.
vault.case_prompt: List each write path and every consumer of cached debt, loss, fee, or strategy valuation.
vault.attacker_goal: Make a stale or incomplete accounting view authorize favorable mint, redeem, fee, or settlement behavior.

vault.title: Permissionless manipulation of an external strategy or collateral
vault.invariant: External integration state used for valuation or solvency cannot be cheaply manipulated by untrusted actors.
vault.case_prompt: Model donation, ERC4626 conversion, oracle dependencies, market liquidity, callbacks, and external admin/config changes.
vault.attacker_goal: Manipulate an external protocol so the vault records false value or incurs unrecoverable loss.

vault.title: Unsupported asset behavior corrupts accounting
vault.invariant: Accounting uses actual received/sent value and handles supported token semantics consistently.
vault.case_prompt: Check fees, rebases, callbacks, blacklists, decimals, return values, and balance-delta assumptions.
vault.attacker_goal: Exploit token behavior to mint unbacked shares, block exits, or desynchronize balances.

lending.title: Prevent or delay liquidation of an unsafe position
lending.invariant: Positions below required solvency can be liquidated within the intended timing and pricing bounds.
lending.case_prompt: Trace health calculation, oracle/config inputs, collateral transferability, pauses, rounding, and liquidation callbacks.
lending.attacker_goal: Shape state so an economically unsafe position remains non-liquidatable.

lending.title: Create or socialize bad debt
lending.invariant: Debt cannot exceed realizable collateral value without explicit bounded loss handling.
lending.case_prompt: Map borrow limits, collateral valuation, interest checkpoints, liquidation incentives, and loss realization.
lending.attacker_goal: Borrow value that cannot be recovered from collateral or the attacker.

lending.title: Manipulate collateral or its exchange rate
lending.invariant: Collateral value used for borrowing and liquidation reflects realizable, manipulation-resistant value.
lending.case_prompt: Inspect ERC4626 donation, thin liquidity, oracle composition, stale rates, decimals, and permissionless external state changes.
lending.attacker_goal: Inflate borrowing power or deflate liquidation value through an external collateral mechanism.

lending.title: Interest or index accounting desynchronization
lending.invariant: Supply, borrow, reserve, and position indexes advance consistently before dependent decisions.
lending.case_prompt: Enumerate lazy updates, alternate entrypoints, rounding, and paths that consume an old index.
lending.attacker_goal: Transact against a stale index to avoid debt or capture unearned value.

lending.title: Extract excess collateral through liquidation
lending.invariant: Liquidation transfers only the collateral justified by repaid debt and configured incentives.
lending.case_prompt: Trace repay/seize units, close factors, rounding, callbacks, and partial liquidation state updates.
lending.attacker_goal: Seize more realizable collateral than the liquidation payment warrants.

bridge.title: Mint or release unbacked destination value
bridge.invariant: Every destination mint/release corresponds to one finalized source lock/burn.
bridge.case_prompt: Trace message identity, finality, replay protection, decimal conversion, refunds, and alternate executors.
bridge.attacker_goal: Cause destination value to be created or released twice or without source backing.

bridge.title: Replay, reorder, or misroute a cross-domain message
bridge.invariant: A message is consumed once, for the intended chain, contract, sender, recipient, and payload.
bridge.case_prompt: Map domain separation, nonce scope, upgrade paths, retries, partial failure, and message normalization.
bridge.attacker_goal: Reuse or redirect an authenticated message for a second favorable state transition.

bridge.title: Permanently strand bridged funds
bridge.invariant: A valid transfer either completes or has a bounded, authorized recovery path.
bridge.case_prompt: Inspect gas/payment quoting, token behavior, recipient restrictions, pause state, retry and refund ownership.
bridge.attacker_goal: Block completion or recovery of other users' funds at acceptable cost.

dex.title: Break reserve or pricing invariant
dex.invariant: Swap, liquidity, and fee transitions preserve the market's defined accounting invariant.
dex.case_prompt: Trace balance observations, callbacks, fee-on-transfer behavior, rounding, hooks, and reserve checkpoints.
dex.attacker_goal: Receive more output or ownership than the supplied economic value permits.

dex.title: Manipulate a price consumed by this or another protocol
dex.invariant: Reported prices represent manipulation-resistant market value over the required horizon.
dex.case_prompt: Map spot/TWAP windows, observation writes, liquidity concentration, flash paths, and downstream consumers.
dex.attacker_goal: Move a consumed price cheaply enough to extract more value elsewhere than manipulation costs.

dex.title: Steal or misattribute liquidity-provider value
dex.invariant: Liquidity ownership, fees, and withdrawals remain proportional to contributed positions.
dex.case_prompt: Inspect position identity, fee checkpoints, donation, callback reentrancy, rounding, and collect/burn ordering.
dex.attacker_goal: Claim principal or fees economically belonging to another liquidity provider.

stablecoin.title: Mint stable value against overstated or insufficient backing
stablecoin.invariant: Every minted stablecoin remains backed by the required collateral value under the configured risk model.
stablecoin.case_prompt: Trace collateral acceptance, oracle normalization, debt ceilings, mint ratios, stale prices, and governance-controlled parameters.
stablecoin.attacker_goal: Mint stablecoins with less real collateral value than the protocol assumes.

stablecoin.title: Redeem for more or better collateral than fair backing allows
stablecoin.invariant: Redemption preserves proportional claim on backing and cannot selectively drain the best collateral.
stablecoin.case_prompt: Map redemption queues, collateral selection, PSM paths, fees, capacity limits, priority rules, and stress behavior.
stablecoin.attacker_goal: Exit through redemption with excess value or leave remaining holders with worse backing.

stablecoin.title: Peg mechanism amplifies rather than absorbs stress
stablecoin.invariant: Mint, burn, redemption, liquidation, and stabilization flows converge toward the intended peg under bounded stress.
stablecoin.case_prompt: Model sell pressure, liquidation timing, arbitrage incentives, mint/redeem cooldowns, caps, and emergency controls.
stablecoin.attacker_goal: Trigger or profit from a feedback loop that pushes the stable asset farther from its peg.

stablecoin.title: Use stale collateral valuation to mint, redeem, or avoid liquidation
stablecoin.invariant: Collateral valuation used for stablecoin decisions is fresh, correctly scaled, and manipulation-resistant.
stablecoin.case_prompt: Inspect oracle freshness checks, decimals, fallback behavior, sequencer status, cached rates, and alternate price paths.
stablecoin.attacker_goal: Transact against an old or mis-scaled price before the protocol observes the true backing value.

perps.title: Amplify oracle error into incorrect PnL or liquidation
perps.invariant: Position PnL, margin, and liquidation decisions use fair mark/index prices within configured bounds.
perps.case_prompt: Trace mark price, index price, TWAP windows, stale oracle handling, spread caps, leverage, and liquidation triggers.
perps.attacker_goal: Move or exploit price input so leveraged PnL or liquidation transfers value incorrectly.

perps.title: Manipulate funding or interest to drain opposing positions
perps.invariant: Funding and borrow rates respond to open interest imbalance without becoming cheaply gameable or divergent.
perps.case_prompt: Map open interest accounting, lazy updates, caps, time weighting, skew changes, settlement, and cross-market effects.
perps.attacker_goal: Create temporary imbalance or stale accounting that pays the attacker more funding than justified.

perps.title: Open positions whose maximum payout exceeds available liquidity
perps.invariant: Protocol liquidity and risk limits cover worst-case owed PnL under the allowed position set.
perps.case_prompt: Inspect max open interest, per-account limits, pool liquidity, unrealized PnL, ADL, bad debt handling, and limit bypass paths.
perps.attacker_goal: Create exposure the protocol cannot pay if price moves favorably for the attacker.

perps.title: Desynchronize margin, collateral, or cross-position accounting
perps.invariant: Account equity, collateral, PnL, fees, and liquidation state remain synchronized across all positions and markets.
perps.case_prompt: Trace partial close, collateral add/remove, isolated versus cross margin, fee accrual, liquidation, and account transfer paths.
perps.attacker_goal: Use one path to preserve usable margin while another path should have consumed or liquidated it.

liquid-staking.title: Misreport or delay staking exchange-rate updates
liquid-staking.invariant: Derivative token exchange rate reflects true underlying stake, rewards, fees, and slashing before dependent exits or transfers.
liquid-staking.case_prompt: Trace reward reporting, slash reporting, oracle authority, rate limits, update cadence, and consumers of cached exchange rate.
liquid-staking.attacker_goal: Enter or exit against a stale or manipulated staking derivative exchange rate.

liquid-staking.title: Manipulate or grief the unstaking withdrawal queue
liquid-staking.invariant: Valid withdrawals progress in the intended order with bounded delay and no cheap priority manipulation.
liquid-staking.case_prompt: Inspect request size limits, batching, cancellation, claim windows, queue ordering, liquidity buffers, and spam economics.
liquid-staking.attacker_goal: Delay other users' exits or jump queue position at acceptable cost.

liquid-staking.title: Exit before slashing or performance loss is fairly socialized
liquid-staking.invariant: Slashing and validator-performance losses are reflected before users can avoid their fair share.
liquid-staking.case_prompt: Map slash detection, report delay, withdrawal finalization, exchange-rate update order, and emergency pause behavior.
liquid-staking.attacker_goal: Withdraw at a pre-loss rate after the loss is economically known but before accounting reflects it.

liquid-staking.title: Validator set or delegation control harms stakers
liquid-staking.invariant: Validator selection and delegation changes cannot route stake to unsafe operators without intended authorization and delay.
liquid-staking.case_prompt: Inspect validator add/remove authority, delegation limits, timelocks, performance accounting, and emergency migration paths.
liquid-staking.attacker_goal: Redirect, censor, or degrade validator-backed assets in a way users cannot avoid or recover from.

governance.title: Capture governance with temporary voting power
governance.invariant: Voting power used for proposals and votes is snapshotted so temporary borrowing cannot decide governance.
governance.case_prompt: Trace proposal threshold, vote power source, checkpoints, delegation, flash-loanability, quorum, and execution delay.
governance.attacker_goal: Borrow or briefly acquire voting power to pass or execute a malicious decision.

governance.title: Bypass or neutralize governance timelock protection
governance.invariant: Sensitive governance actions remain delayed long enough for users and guardians to react.
governance.case_prompt: Map proposer/executor roles, emergency paths, upgrade calls, queued calldata, cancellation, delay changes, and nested governance actions.
governance.attacker_goal: Execute a sensitive change before the intended warning or exit period has elapsed.

governance.title: Execute proposal calldata whose effects differ from governance intent
governance.invariant: Executed proposal actions match the reviewed target, value, calldata, and described protocol change.
governance.case_prompt: Inspect batching, delegatecall, proxy upgrades, calldata encoding, target allowlists, value transfers, and description/hash binding.
governance.attacker_goal: Hide or redirect a privileged action inside apparently benign governance execution.

governance.title: Emergency or guardian role overrides normal governance
governance.invariant: Emergency powers are bounded to intended safety actions and cannot permanently seize value or governance control.
governance.case_prompt: List every guardian/admin action, pause/unpause asymmetry, upgrade authority, parameter scope, recovery paths, and revocation rules.
governance.attacker_goal: Use a privileged fast path to bypass governance for a non-emergency value-moving change.
